La presenza allo stadio non cambia la protesta; sui social arrivano critiche dopo il comunicato.

I tifosi della Lazio torneranno all’Olimpico per due partite, senza interrompere la protesta contro la società. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Il messaggio riportato dal Messaggero esclude una tregua politica: il rientro sugli spalti non cambia la posizione nei confronti di Lotito.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that la scelta è di sostenere la squadra in due gare casalinghe. Nel messaggio, però, viene precisato che «non si torna indietro»: la presenza allo stadio non equivale a una riconciliazione con la società.

It has been revealed that la valutazione della gestione di Lotito resta immutata: «Gestione inadeguata, distanza siderale dal calcio moderno, necessità di un cambiamento ormai improrogabile». Al ritorno dei tifosi non si accompagna, dunque, alcuno sconto sulle ragioni della contestazione.

In a recent development, sui social, la strategia ha suscitato anche critiche. Tra i commenti comparsi dopo il comunicato ricorre l’obiezione: «Sono solo giustificazioni per mantenere il punto dopo il dietrofront».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ardon Jashari, centrocampista del Milan, è presente in conferenza stampa, a partire dalle ore 19:00, alla vigilia di Olympiacos-Milan, sfida valida per la quinta giornata della League Phase di Europa League e in programma domani alle 18.45 allo stadio Georgios Karaiskakis di Atene.

Segui in diretta le dichiarazioni del centrocampista rossonero con il live testuale su MilanNews.it.

In a recent development, stai tornando ad essere quel calciatore che abbiamo visto a Brugge? "Mi piace anche essere quel tipo di giocatore che può aiutare la squadra anche con la mia personalità in campo. Se confrontiamo, per esempio, ora le competizioni, per noi come squadra e anche per ogni giocatore come me, è importante vincere le partite e finora l'abbiamo fatto molto bene in Serie A. Ora è una competizione diversa che iniziamo, questa è la verità. E domani è una grande, grande opportunità, ma anche, diciamo, c'è una sorta di pressione per tutti noi. E penso che la partita contro il Frosinone sia la Serie A, è una competizione diversa, ma comunque per tutti i giocatori, ha portato buon umore, una buona atmosfera e domani dobbiamo essere pronti a a competere e a vincere la partita".

Industry observers note that domani affronterai Freuler, tuo compagno di Nazionale "Avrò un'extra motivazione. Abbiamo parlato di questa partita mentre eravamo in Nazionale. Non vede l'ora di giocare contro di noi ed anche io non vedo l'ora di giocare contro di lui. Sarà una grande partita. Non vedo l'ora di incontrarlo e di batterlo".

It has been revealed that ti sei acceso domenica: qual è il tuo livello adesso? Cosa puoi dare ancora? "Buona domanda. So che posso fare molto meglio. Penso che adesso la gara contro il Frosinone è stata una buona partita per me, ma non è il livello che voglio mostrare. Ma sto lavorando ogni giorno per essere la versione migliore di se, così che club, allenatore e tifosi possano vedere cosa sono in grado fare".

Industry observers note that in cosa stai lavorando, su quali aspetti? "Nel passato, dove ho già giocato, avevo un ruolo centrale in squadra, o nell'undici iniziale. Quindi giocavo sempre. Penso che con il Milan devo imparare ad essere pronto anche se non gioco sempre, ed è una cosa che non ho sviluppato in passato. Spero che in un momento spero di essere così decisivo anche nel Milan".

- Ore 20.01 Finisce qui la conferenza stampa di Ardon Jashari.

Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere. Prendiamo il punto, ne abbiamo 10 in classifica e in fin dei conti è un buon risultato per andare avanti. Ricordo un loro calcio d’angolo e i due gol, in questo momento gli avversari sono cinici davanti alla porta. C’è poco da fare, accettiamo il punto e andiamo avanti. L’impatto sui giocatori? In questo momento va un po’ così, le prime dieci partite siamo stati sempre noi a sbloccare, mentre ora sono gli avversari a farlo. Non credo che abbia un impatto sulla fiducia dei calciatori, devi correre un po’ di più se sei in svantaggio, ma abbiamo lottato fino alla fine e serve alzare l’asticella. Non dobbiamo subire questi gol, basta vedere le statistiche a nostro favore. C’è uno squilibrio tra le occasioni create e i gol segnati. Anche Cherki ha detto che mancava energia? Siamo stati molto aggressivi. I due terzini in posizione centrale? Abbiamo iniziato con Bouaddi e Enzo in mezzo per vedere se potevamo trovare equilibrio, poi Nico e Matheus Nunes hanno fatto bene, è un’altra opzione per noi. Volevamo fare qualche cambio ed essere più fisici in mezzo al campo per contrastarli. La qualità del gol di Cherki? Ottimo, sono contento per lui. Ha fatto bene, sappiamo che sa giocare meglio centralmente, ma sta facendo bene. Ci aspettavamo un Napoli col blocco basso, era difficile trovare soluzioni, ma dovevamo evitare di concedere i gol concessi, erano evitabili. I cori a Donnarumma? Non ci ho fatto caso, ero concentrato sulla partita. Era difficile attaccare il Napoli, erano in undici sulla linea dell’area. Potevamo fare meglio nelle chance avute e cercare di evitare le due occasioni concesse. Hanno avuto quelle e il corner di Beukema, c’è rammarico per non aver vinto, ma se non puoi farlo è importante anche non perdere. Non vinciamo da tre partite, ma i meriti del Napoli sono importanti: si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni. Noi potevamo fare meglio, il Napoli ha avuto i suoi meriti e ha fatto una buona gara”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:25 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 21 November 2026.

Wouter Vrancken remarked Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

The 47-year-old said: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

According to recent reports, 'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

He said: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and highlights grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

La Lazio non ha espresso una preferenza; alle precedenti elezioni fu l’unico club di Serie A ad astenersi.

Almeno 11 club di Serie A sostengono Giovanni Malagò nella corsa alla presidenza della FIGC, mentre Adriano Galliani raccoglie il sostegno di un altro fronte. Secondo quanto riportato da Calcio e Finanza, La Lega Serie A, che alle precedenti elezioni aveva promosso la candidatura dell’ex numero uno del CONI con uno schieramento compatto, rischia di uscire dalla nuova tornata elettorale divisa al proprio interno.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il numero dei club favorevoli a Malagò è rilevante per la sua candidatura: per presentarla serve infatti l’appoggio di almeno una componente. Il fronte pro Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista, potrebbe dunque trovarsi in minoranza.

In a recent development, la scelta del prossimo presidente federale resta aperta tra i due candidati. La divisione nella massima serie riguarda anche gli equilibri interni della Lega in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali.

Secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport, alcuni club si sono allontanati dallo schieramento favorevole a Malagò, Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra le società ancora indecise figurano anche Juventus e Milan.

Alle differenze sulla presidenza della FIGC potrebbe quindi aggiungersi un’ulteriore frattura al momento di eleggere i consiglieri federali. È su entrambi i passaggi che si misura la compattezza mostrata dalla Serie A nella precedente tornata.

  • Il cambio di marcia è evidente nei numeri: nelle ultime nove presenze tra club e nazionale Alvarez è stato coinvolto in nove reti, con cinque gol e quattro assist.
  • La sua evoluzione passa anche da una maggiore integrazione nel progetto.

Sembrava un rapporto destinato a finire nel peggiore dei modi, quello tra Julian Alvarez e l'Atletico Madrid. Dopo il desiderio espresso in estate di trasferirsi al Barcellona, l'attaccante argentino è rimasto a nella capitale in un clima tutt'altro che sereno, tra dubbi sul futuro, tensioni e qualche contestazione da parte dei tifosi. Anche il rendimento iniziale non aveva aiutato: appena due gol nelle prime tredici partite avevano alimentato le critiche, soprattutto dopo gli errori contro il Barcellona nella sconfitta per 2-1. Nelle ultime settimane, però, il campione del mondo ha cambiato passo e sta ritrovando il ruolo centrale nelle idee di Diego Simeone.

Il cambio di marcia è evidente nei numeri: nelle ultime nove presenze tra club e nazionale Alvarez è stato coinvolto in nove reti, con cinque gol e quattro assist. La sosta internazionale gli ha restituito fiducia, grazie alla rete contro l'Uruguay e alla doppietta realizzata contro il Costa Rica, prima della conferma arrivata con due assist nella vittoria dell'Atlético sul Getafe. A colpire non è soltanto la produzione offensiva, ma soprattutto il modo in cui l'argentino partecipa alla manovra. Più mobile, preciso e presente tra le linee, Alvarez riesce a incidere anche senza trovare direttamente la via della rete. Contro il Getafe ha creato quattro occasioni, il dato migliore della gara, completando 19 passaggi nella metà campo avversaria.

La sua evoluzione passa anche da una maggiore integrazione nel progetto. I movimenti in profondità e gli abbassamenti favoriscono gli inserimenti di giocatori come Alex Baena, Pablo Barrios e Kang-in Lee, rendendolo un elemento prezioso nell'attacco dell'Atletico. L'argentino è stato coinvolto direttamente in sei delle ultime nove reti segnate dai Colchoneros in tutte le competizioni. Anche fuori dal campo qualcosa sembra essere cambiato: dopo le tensioni estive legate al mancato trasferimento, avrebbe deciso di interrompere il rapporto con il suo agente Fernando Hidalgo, valutando un nuovo percorso professionale. Inoltre, nonostante le voci di mercato, non ci sarebbero segnali di una partenza già a gennaio.

Resta però un ultimo passo per riconquistare completamente il pubblico del Metropolitano: tornare a segnare con continuità. E magari essere decisivo il 2 dicembre al Camp Nou, per dimostrare che l'Atletico può lottare per il titolo insieme alle due superpotenze del calcio spagnolo.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

It has been revealed that brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

In a recent development, “I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick remarked. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a major game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick mentioned. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

Recent findings suggest that “We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Sources indicate that gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react promptly enough.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

“We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that “We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he remarked. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that amici e amiche di MilanNews.it, ben ritrovati.
  • - La conferenza, inizialmente prevista alle 19.00, inizierà con qualche minuto di ritardo.
  • Cosa chiede alla squadra per domani?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that amici e amiche di MilanNews.it, ben ritrovati. Ruben Amorim è pronto per presentare Olympiacos-Milan in conferenza stampa. L'allenatore portoghese parlerà dalla pancia dello stadio Georgios Karaiskakis al Pireo, dove domani sera i rossoneri affronteranno i greci in un match valido per la quinta giornata della fase campionato di Europa League. Tra le fila del Diavolo ci sono ben 9 assenti, ma è inutile ribadire quanto sia importante vincere per cominciare a dare un senso alla classifica europea del Milan. Rimanete con noi ed il nostro live testuale per seguire tutte le dichiarazioni di Amorim in conferenza.

- La conferenza, inizialmente prevista alle 19.00, inizierà con qualche minuto di ritardo.

Cosa chiede alla squadra per domani? Più volume in attacco? Come pensa di sostenere Ramos? "Non è aituare Ramos, ma anche Camarda e tutti quelli che giocano davanti. È un fatto che dobbiamo migliorare nell'ultimo terzo. L'unica cosa che possiamo fare è migliorare i principi. Dobbiamo migliorare in queste piccole cose, e solo così so aiutare i miei giocatori. Contro l'Olympiacos sarà duna partita diversa rispetto a quella contro il Frosinone, così come sarà diversa rispetto a quella contro il Cagliari. Dobbiamo migliorare, anche nel modo di difendere. Abbiamo quasi sempre subito un gol, quindi è un'altra cosa che dobbiamo migliorare".

It has been revealed that come descriveresti l'Olympiacos come squadra? "Grazie per l'accoglienza. È una squadra forte. Sono aggressivi, soprattutto in casa. Ho giocato qua due volte ed è stata complicata per me. Conosco il loro allenatore, cosa vuole fare, giocano compatto, un calcio positivo, 4-3-3, cambia tanto, fa rotazioni, ha Jota, tanti giocatori portoghesi. È una squadra forte, e con i loro tifosi presenti sarà una partita complicata. Chiquinho un grande talento, ma molto impulsivo. Spero che domani giochi bene ma spero che abbia ancora una grande carriera davanti a luI".

Il processo di crescita del Milan passa anche dall'Europa? "Per essere una buona squadra devi fare bene sia in campionato che in Europa. Solo così si può essere una buona squadra. Dobbiamo esserlo, soprattutto al Milan. I complimenti? Sto aspettando sempre le cose quando adranno male, perché non ci vuole granché a cambiare la situazione. È questo quello che sto cercando di far capire ai miei giocatori, perché non andrà sempre così. Siamo all'inizio di un processo, e penso che abbiamo bisogno di tutti. Abbiamo perso Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, e tutti devono essere pronti, perché non ci sono scuse nei grandi club. Dobbiamo essere pronti per questo. Non posso credere che abbiamo perso tutte queste partite in Europa perché abbiamo fatto rotazioni. Dobbiamo essere sempre pronti, ed affrontare le partite come contro l'Inter, il Frosinone, il Genova. Stiamo costruendo tante cose. Domani è un altro test per noi. Credo in tutte le competizioni, se possiamo vincerle tutte no. Scudetto? Non ho cambiato idea. Quest'anno è difficile, ma se abbiamo la possibilità di lottare lo faremo. Non cambierò per i complimenti, perché aspetto ed anche voi state aspettando (le critiche, ndr). Domani dobbiamo vincere, perché se non lo facessimo...sono pronto per questo".

Il calcio sta diventando pericoloso per la salute mentale e fisica di calciatori ed allenatori? "È difficile proteggere il giocatore considerando il momento che stiamo vivendo. I più giovani saranno più pronti a convivere con le critiche. È diverso rispetto alla mia realtà. È difficile controllare questo. Quando mi avete chiesto di GTA, preferirei che i miei giocatori giocassero tutti i giorno piuttosto che scrollare i social. Cosa voglio intendere è che noi vogliamo più tempo tra le partite. Parlo del prodotto, non della mia vita. Parlo della qualità del prodotto del calcio. Non so cosa intendesse Fabregas, ma è l'evoluzione della società, del calcio, che è un business, e dobbiamo essere pronti. I social media, e tutte questa roba, è molto difficile per i calciatori, che comunque convivono con più critiche rispetto a quanto faccio io. Dopo il Frosinone non ho letto niente, perché è così che voglio vivere la mia vita".

Da calciatore hai una grande esperienza: cosa ti aspetti dallo stadio domani? "Conosco l'atmosfera qui. È pazzesca. È importante per i miei calciatori avere questa esperienza, anche se non c'è stadio più difficile di San Siro dove giocare. In questi tipi di stadi dobbiamo essere pronti. Abbiamo perso 5-1 una volta, ma sono molto focus su quello che bisogna fare, come cominceremo la partita, su queste cose sono concentrato. L'ambiente dovrebbe essere normale per questi giocatori, abituati ai grandi scenari. Dobbiamo essere competitivi e pronti".

- 20.01 Finisce qui la conferenza stampa di Ruben Amorim.

MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.
  • And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

It has been revealed that messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers.

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top.

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up substantial-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Industry observers note that jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

Sources indicate that it was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Industry observers note that djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park.

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

According to recent reports, the South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

Industry observers note that an initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

It has been revealed that motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side.

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

It has been revealed that naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

Recent findings suggest that it shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

Dopo il pari del Napoli per 2-2 contro il Manchester, Giovane ha parlato così in mixed zone:.

“Noi sapevamo che era una partita difficile oggi, il Manchester City è una delle migliori squadre del mondo, quindi il mister ha parlato con tutti noi per entrare con la testa giusta e fare una buona prestazione. È un peccato che abbiamo pareggiato, però è un punto importante per perseguire i nostri obiettivi. Penso che noi abbiamo fatto una buona gara, una buona prestazione. Adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti perché domenica c’è un’altra partita in Serie A. Adesso è già finita e dobbiamo pensare avanti. Qualunque sia il modulo tattico con cui giochiamo, sappiamo quello che dobbiamo fare. Ovviamente si cambia qualcosa quando si cambia modulo, ma penso che anche l’ultima vittoria ci abbia aiutato a prendere fiducia per affrontare oggi questa partita. Giocare qui è difficilissimo perché il Manchester City è una squadra forte. Sappiamo che adesso stanno attraversando un momento difficile, ma non smettono di essere il Manchester City e anche noi non smettiamo di essere il Napoli, quindi è questo. La risposta è quella di sempre, che noi abbiamo quella voglia, quella fame, quella grinta di vincere, è questo. Speriamo che domenica possiamo vincere. Sì, può essere, perché se vinciamo e conquistiamo tre punti così cambia tutto, però anche un punto in una partita come quella di questa sera è importante. La Champions è una competizione difficile, ma adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti e perseguire i nostri obiettivi”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il presidente della Lazio punta a tornare nell’incarico; per i tre posti si presentano anche gli uscenti e Sticchi Damiani.

La Serie A eleggerà tre consiglieri federali il 14 dicembre, ma i candidati sono cinque. Ai tre uscenti Stefano Campoccia, Giorgio Chiellini e Giuseppe Marotta si sono aggiunti Saverio Sticchi Damiani e il presidente della Lazio Claudio Lotito. Tra le ipotesi in vista del voto c’è anche quella di preferenze disgiunte tra la presidenza FIGC e il Consiglio federale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nel breve mandato di Malagò, i posti spettanti alla massima serie erano occupati da Campoccia, dell’Udinese, Chiellini, della Juventus, e Marotta, dell’Inter. Tutti e tre si sono ricandidati. Con loro correranno il presidente del Lecce Sticchi Damiani e Lotito, che punta a tornare nell’incarico già ricoperto.

Come riferisce il Corriere dello Sport, il quadro delle candidature si inserisce in una Serie A attraversata da divisioni. Alcuni club sono usciti dal fronte Malagò, con Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra gli indecisi figurano anche Juventus e Milan; in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali, le fratture interne potrebbero allargarsi.

Industry observers note that ogni società di Serie A può indicare un candidato al Consiglio federale. Nelle precedenti elezioni Chiellini aveva ottenuto sette voti e Marotta sei, in una situazione descritta come praticamente opposta a quella attuale.

Recent findings suggest that il fronte favorevole a Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista Marotta, potrebbe risentire della propria posizione di minoranza. I club che sostengono Malagò sono almeno 11: un sostegno necessario alla sua candidatura, per la quale serve l’appoggio di almeno una componente.

In questo scenario, alcune società potrebbero scegliere il voto disgiunto: sostenere un candidato alla presidenza FIGC e, per il Consiglio federale, esprimere una preferenza per un nome non apertamente schierato con lui. L’esempio indicato è un voto per Malagò alla presidenza e per Marotta, primo sostenitore di Galliani, come consigliere. Una soluzione che richiederebbe un lavoro diplomatico.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:22 EST, 21 November 2026.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes praised his side for having the mentality to grind out last-gasp winners and hailed their late victory over Motherwell as a ‘top-class performance’.

McInnes admits he would have liked a more comfortable evening from a match which saw his side fire 29 shots with 11 on target, but he was happy with the level of chance creation and delighted to see Ryan Naderi serve up yet another crucial goal with a deflected effort that made the difference two minutes from time.

Rangers had opened brightly with a Manny Fernandez goal on eight minutes, but looked like sliding to a third straight league draw away from home after Jake Girdwood-Reich had levelled for the home side in the first half.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I thought it was a very good, strong performance. I’ve just been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot,’ remarked McInnes, whose men are four points behind Celtic with a game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, ‘I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week. It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance.

‘Away from home in the Premiership, you’re never going to dominate a whole game. There were little spells Motherwell had on transitions, but our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time.

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic.

‘Equally, on the sidelines, I felt a goal was coming. It’s OK me feeling that, but I think the players feel it too and it’s important they do. It would have been such a body blow if we hadn’t found a winning goal, given the stats and the performance.

‘It’s a tough away game and it’s the first time we’ve won here in three years, so that illustrates that.

‘When we pick the bones out of it, there will be a lot of what we ask for in that game.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how vital they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an issue for my side.

Sources indicate that ‘On this fantastic run, we’ve been very strong. We were by far the better team. We dominated the chances and a lot of what I was hoping for was there.

‘It was just that execution. We’ve had this story before, but, as long as we keep winning, I’m all right with that.

In a recent development, ‘I’m getting asked about not putting teams to bed. That’s another away game with two goals. It’s four in a row now. In our last two home games, we’ve scored four and three, so scoring goals isn’t really causing a problem, even if people are looking for a negative.

‘I think that performance was an improvement from where we’ve been in recent weeks.’.

McInnes also reserved special praise for matchwinner Naderi.

‘Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,’ said the manager. ‘Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in.

‘His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a substantial horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure, but he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most key position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball.

Manny Fernandez opened the scoring for the Ibrox men in the 2-1 victory.

‘He led the line brilliantly. It was a proper No 9 performance.

Naderi admits he is delighted to be scoring messy goals that are making a real impact on his side’s challenge for the title.

It has been revealed that ‘I like those games. Of course we would like to win 3-0, but, when you win in the last minute, that's something special,’ said the Czech internationalist.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’.

Motherwell head coach Alfred Johansson noted: ‘It is obviously tough to concede that goal at the very end. We had a feeling we could finish the game with a draw.

It has been revealed that ‘I think Rangers were better than us. They had a good start to the game and it was tough for us conceding a goal from a set-piece when we are not aggressive enough.

‘At the end, we lost the energy. Rangers were turning up the heat in the last 15, 20 minutes. We were fighting and surviving and then they scored.

Sources indicate that ‘Alex Paulsen played fantastic in goal. He has been making a lot of saves for us this season and, at the end, it is tough for him to concede a goal like that.’.

E ha sfiorato il grande colpo. Il palleggio del City lo ha scalfito ma non è riuscito a scardinare la sua organizzazione. Spazi occupati e reattività alla base della guerriglia organizzata da Allegri, che esce da Manchester con un’ottima notizia: la squadra lo segue, è dalla sua parte”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.
  • The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Industry observers note that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I stated, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

Latest Update: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

It has been revealed that this must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

It has been revealed that so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Sources indicate that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba mentioned. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

According to recent reports, floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Sources indicate that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca mentioned. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Industry observers note that allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca mentioned.

It has been revealed that cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

According to recent reports, erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

In a recent development, FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

It has been revealed that great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Recent findings suggest that well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

Industry observers note that A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Sources indicate that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Recent findings suggest that lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

In a recent development, significant cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

According to recent reports, norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Sources indicate that norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Sources indicate that maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

It has been revealed that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

According to recent reports, credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

Recent findings suggest that A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

Sources indicate that and the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Recent findings suggest that another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Industry observers note that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

It has been revealed that yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Industry observers note that kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

It has been revealed that norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It has been revealed that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

Industry observers note that 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

It has been revealed that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

Industry observers note that city fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY.

Manchester City or Norwich vs Brighton.

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Recent findings suggest that philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Dopo dieci anni al Manchester City, il tecnico scelse di fermarsi; ora considera un incarico da commissario tecnico.

Recent findings suggest that pep Guardiola disse no alla panchina dell'Italia la scorsa estate. L'allenatore spagnolo, 55 anni, lo ha raccontato a Romário TV, il programma YouTube condotto dall'ex fuoriclasse brasiliano. Per la prima volta ha parlato pubblicamente dei contatti con la Federcalcio e delle ragioni per cui non è arrivato alla Nazionale azzurra.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

A presentargli una proposta ufficiale furono Paolo Maldini e Leonardo, ex bandiere del Milan. Guardiola ha confermato di aver parlato con loro: «Ne parlo per la prima volta, ma sì, ho parlato con loro. Ero quasi in imbarazzo nel dire di no all'Italia».

According to recent reports, la possibilità di guidare gli azzurri lo attirava molto. Il tecnico ha spiegato quanto avrebbe significato per lui accettare l'incarico: «Sarebbe stato uno dei più grandi onori della mia carriera allenare la nazionale italiana».

Alla base del rifiuto c'era la stanchezza. Guardiola arrivava da dieci anni al Manchester City, durante i quali aveva conquistato sei campionati e una Champions League. Alle spalle aveva inoltre 18 anni complessivi in panchina, scanditi da partite ogni tre giorni.

Industry observers note that sentiva così il bisogno di prendersi una pausa. Nel raccontare quella decisione, ha detto: «Mi sono reso conto che dovevo smettere. Avevo bisogno di un po' di tempo per me stesso».

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026.

All eyes will be on Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Sources indicate that liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they right now sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

United have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United right now sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool).

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

According to recent reports, the 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

In a recent development, the Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool).

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

Industry observers note that the 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool).

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

In a recent development, but across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Industry observers note that manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular concern since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool).

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating major chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four massive chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United).

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

According to recent reports, the 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an crucial role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a big chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool).

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the big-money move from Newcastle.

Isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent major chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

Left forward – Cody Gakpo (Liverpool).

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United reveals just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one big chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

Sofascore's combined XI for United's huge trip to Liverpool this afternoon.

Il processo di crescita del Milan passa anche dall'Europa? "Per essere una buona squadra devi fare bene sia in campionato che in Europa. Solo così si può essere una buona squadra. Dobbiamo esserlo, soprattutto al Milan. I complimenti? Sto aspettando sempre le cose quando adranno male, perché non ci vuole granché a cambiare la situazione. Abbiamo perso Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, e tutti devono essere pronti, perché non ci sono scuse nei grandi club. Dobbiamo essere pronti per questo. Non posso credere che abbiamo perso tutte queste partite in Europa perché abbiamo fatto rotazioni. Dobbiamo essere sempre pronti, ed affrontare le partite come contro l'Inter, il Frosinone, il Genova. Stiamo costruendo tante cose. Domani è un altro test per noi. Credo in tutte le competizioni, se possiamo vincerle tutte no.

Recent findings suggest that scudetto? Non ho cambiato idea. Quest'anno è difficile, ma se abbiamo la possibilità di lottare lo faremo.
