Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026.

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he stated.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

In a recent development, ‘Yeah, exactly,’ he remarked. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

It has been revealed that ‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

It has been revealed that ‘Especially for the latest guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

Industry observers note that ‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

It has been revealed that come descriveresti l'Olympiacos come squadra? "Grazie per l'accoglienza. È una squadra forte. Sono aggressivi, soprattutto in casa. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Sempre Con Te è intervenuto Enzo Bucchioni: “Un voto alto per il Napoli, la miglior partita stagionale.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Sempre Con Te è intervenuto Enzo Bucchioni: “Un voto alto per il Napoli, la miglior partita stagionale. Lo aspettavamo così dall’inizio. Una prestazione inattesa, finalmente però si è ritrovato l’orgoglio di una grande squadra. Si era visto in stagione qualche sprazzo di Napoli convincente. Il pareggio con il City ha un sapore differente. Non era atteso, può essere questa la ripartenza vera? C’è da augurarsi di sì. Le prossime sono alla portata. Il Napoli deve segnare di più e subire di meno? Secondo me subire di meno. È mancato il sacrificio degli attaccanti. Se non danno una mano per primi, qualsiasi fase difensiva va in difficoltà. È uscito Lang, la fase difensiva non la faceva, era pigro. Quando perdi palla devi andare con determinazione sul pallone ed è successo. La fase difensiva non funzionava per questo. Le squadre di Allegri hanno sempre avuto queste caratteristiche, ma non riusciva a farsi capire. Come vedo le parole di Allegri su De Bruyne? La posizione di De Bruyne la sappiamo, gli piace un altro calcio. Spero che contro il City si sia divertito, penso che ci sia stato anche un confronto. Un allenatore che si sbilancia lo vedo come segnale importante. Allegri ha ripreso la barca, quel tipo di calcio con il baricentro basso e rincorse all’indietro non faccia parte del bagaglio di molti giocatori. Anche Allegri ha provato a fare altre cose, ma non gli erano riuscite. Ieri abbiamo visto Allegri con la faccia giusta”.

  • Eccetto il passaggio a vuoto ieri contro l'AEK Atene, Couto sta dimostrando una crescita progressiva rilevante.

In a recent development, yan Couto ha quasi tutti i requisiti che il Como stava cercando per occupare con maggiore qualità e dinamismo la casella del terzino destro. La partenza di Vojvoda e il rinnovo di Smolcic hanno spinto la dirigenza lariana a trovare un nuovo innesto di peso per potenziare la fascia in questione e alla fine hanno puntato su una scommessa che per due stagioni di fila era rimasta nell'ombra di Ryerson al Borussia Dortmund. Mentre al Sinigaglia e con Cesc Fabregas in panchina sta ritrovando la miglior versione di se stesso.

Facile che il brasiliano classe 2002 possa superare quanto prima l'impiego avuto nel BVB. D'altronde la scorsa stagione ha raggiunto 1501 minuti tra tutte le competizioni, mentre nel 2024/25 quasi 1400. Oggi, in prestito al Como, il tecnico catalano ha già utilizzato Couto per 1247 minuti in campo tra Serie A e Champions League: difficilmente ci rinuncia, anche perché il suo peso è evidente quando la squadra ha il pallino del gioco e dà libero sfogo al suo calcio. Non a caso in proiezione offensiva rende al massimo e alla sua prima avventura nella massima serie italiana ha confezionato 4 assist in 11 partite, con il destro vellutato che si ritrova. Al Girona di Michel (2023/24) la sua massima espressione nel regalare palle gol ai compagni: 10 passaggi chiave in 34 partite di LaLiga. Il suo record personale assoluto in carriera.

Eccetto il passaggio a vuoto ieri contro l'AEK Atene, Couto sta dimostrando una crescita progressiva rilevante. Sorge spontanea la domanda: quanto fatto varrà la conferma del Como? Il terzino brasiliano è arrivato in estate dal Borussia Dortmund in prestito con diritto di riscatto: siamo quasi a dicembre, perciò il primo bilancio la dirigenza lariana comincerà a farlo. Di certo il 24enne di Curitiba si gioca tantissimo del suo futuro, dopo aver ritrovato una realtà confortevole e che lo esalti, questo anche grazie a Fabregas e al gioco espresso dalla squadra. Di certo servirà sborsare 20-22 milioni di euro al termine della stagione se la volontà sarà quella di trattenerlo sul Lario.

Breaking: Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1268 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to strategy.

Industry observers note that it’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Industry observers note that yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for key goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

Not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

Sources indicate that first in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

Both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

That’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Sources indicate that fernandez revealed himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

Industry observers note that A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He revealed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

In a recent development, in his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

He put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

According to recent reports, mcInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil stated after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

It has been revealed that MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

In a recent development, RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”.

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o.

Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” claims Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

Industry observers note that “It really is about the hooligan era,” notes a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Recent findings suggest that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at Latest Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

According to recent reports, mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police mentioned that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

According to recent reports, just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno stated: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

In a recent development, on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

In a recent development, riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

In a recent development, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

According to recent reports, the Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Industry observers note that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Sources indicate that since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

According to recent reports, much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

Al Martelli è festa biancorossa. Un Mantova sul velluto si sbarazza dell'Arezzo grazie alle reti di Spinaccè nel primo tempo, Kouda e Bragantini nella ripresa. La squadra di Modesto torna a vincere dopo diversi passi falsi e fa un grande balzo in avanti, stazionandosi in quarta posizione. Sempre più invischiato l'Arezzo di Bucchi.

Bardi 6 - In una gara in cui ha tutto da rimetterci, è richiamato sull'attenti dal destro di Tavernelli, per poi tornare ad appisolarsi.

Tomasevic 6,5 - Segue a ruota l'uomo in marcatura. Dà un'alternativa in avanti con la torre per Bragantini e proponendosi perfino sul tre a zero.

It has been revealed that cella 6 - Il cambio di valutazione sulla sanzione fa si che ci sia anche la prossima. In questa non corre alcun rischio.

In a recent development, castellini 6 - Il primo sussulto del match è il suo. Con il piede che ha, non è un caso essere uno dei migliori assist-man della squadra.

Industry observers note that radaelli 6 - Contenitivo. Senza grossi spunti, ma fa buona guardia su Righetti, più offensivo. Dal 57' Del Lungo 6 - Esattamente come il sostituto.

Trimboli 6 - In mezzo ai corridori, serve qualcuno che dia maggior equilibrio. Non è sinonimo di staticità; affatto: soffia la sfera nell'area opposta quando ormai la gara è già archiviata.

Kouda 8 - Break a spezzare in due il centrocampo dell'Arezzo per poi servire il compagno, a segno. Tocco geniale per Spinaccè e glaciale dagli undici metri per il primo rigore in carriera.

Benaissa 7 - Un pendolino sulla corsia mancina. Il tema è lo stesso: profondità e pallone a rimorchio, generando di fatto il gol del tre a zero. Dal 86' Kospo s.v.

According to recent reports, bragantini 8 - Ha una marcia in più. Spartisce la palma di migliore in campo con Kouda, trascinando i suoi a suon di gol e giocate. Dal 79' Cajazzo s.v.

Industry observers note that ruocco 5,5 - Stenta a entrare in partita, complice l'eccessiva euforia del suo compagno di reparto. Porta pressione e strappa la sfera a Nunziante, ma poi lo grazia. Dal 57' Ignacchiti 6 - Entra con determinazione, seppur non vada sopra le righe.

Spinaccè 7,5 - Prima titolarità da incorniciare. Risponde presente fin da subito stappando la partita, per poi procurarsi il penalty del doppio vantaggio. Dal 86' Vlahovic s.v.

Recent findings suggest that allenatore: Modesto 7 - Il suo Mantova torna a vincere e lo fa in grande stile. Azzecca la scelta di Spinaccè dal 1' e mantiene il controllo di una gara quasi mai messa in discussione.

It has been revealed that nunziante 5 - Se la parata a inizio gara su Castellini poteva influire in positivo, ecco che nella ripresa ne combina di ogni. Il portiere si sa essere ricordato per le sviste.

Renzi 5,5 - Partita ordinata fino a quando Benaissa non decide di alzare i giri del motore.

Gilli 5,5 - Concede troppo spazio a Spinaccè, che poi fa tutto il resto.

Coppolaro 6,5 - Se vi state chiedendo il perchè con i tre gol presi abbia un giudizio così alto basta andare a vedere i due salvataggi sulla linea.

Recent findings suggest that righetti 5 - Propositivo in avanti e perfino pericoloso. In fase difensiva, però, Bragantini lo salta di netto.

Industry observers note that sala 6 - S'invola e regala al compagno un cioccolatino solo da scartare. Una bella sgroppata offensiva in una gara in cui è richiamato alla corsa indietro.

Napoli-Milan, prezzi e info per la vendita dei tagliandi

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
  • La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.
  • It has been revealed that la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

It has been revealed that la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

In a recent development, ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/.

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

Recent findings suggest that I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

Questi i prezzi della Tribuna Family:.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE).

Industry observers note that dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM.

Dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

FASE 2 – ISCRIZIONE PREMIUM SSC NAPOLI.

Industry observers note that dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

In a recent development, in caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

Per maggiori informazioni sulla modalità Passbook consultare questo link (si apre in una nuova scheda).

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita è vietata ai residenti nella regione Lombardia, ad eccezione dei possessori di Fidelity Card SSC Napoli emessa entro il 1° settembre 2026.

I biglietti potranno essere acquistati:.

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card);.

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il link per l’acquisto online dei titoli d’ingresso è disponibile qui. (si apre in una nuova scheda).

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card).

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Non è possibile usufruire della modalità di acquisto presso i punti vendita.

Il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo – stampa termica (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

L’elenco dei punti vendita è disponibile qui.

In nessun caso sarà consentito il cambio utilizzatore per i biglietti acquistati.

Industry observers note that si raccomanda di non acquistare i tagliandi in circuiti o canali web diversi da quelli ufficiali e indicati in questo comunicato. La SSC Napoli non risponde di eventuali frodi subite a seguito di acquisti effettuati al di fuori dei canali autorizzati. Inoltre, ogni abuso e/o utilizzo fraudolento dei biglietti sarà punito ai termini di legge.

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita dei biglietti potrebbe essere soggetta a limitazioni territoriali.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/.

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD).

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 13:39 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:49 EST, 22 November 2026.

Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

Sources indicate that ‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he said. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday.

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week.

‘They are a very good team, and that has given us the belief that we can go to the next round. It’s crucial to take it game-by-game, though. This is the most important one. If we can get the points we can go on from there, step-by-step.’.

According to recent reports, torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite at the moment sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

In a recent development, ‘We are playing against a Portuguese second division team but we have to be focused and aggressive,’ warned Yang. ‘They are higher than us in the Europa League table. They’ve already won two matches so they will be a good team.

Industry observers note that ‘We have to approach it the same way as we would playing a team like Benfica or Sporting Lisbon. We have to go there and try to win. If we play like we did against St Mirren, we can do it.’.

Meanwhile, Yang is adamant that being made exempt from military service wasn’t even on his mind as South Korea won the Asian Games this year.

Played in Japan in September and October, Yang’s side defeated the hosts 1-0 in the final.

That meant all the South Korean players were no longer obliged to spend time serving in the military before they turn 28.

Yang, 24, who suffered a hamstring injury in the opening victory against Qatar, reflected: ‘It was great. Obviously, it was nice to win it but I also got injured, which was unfortunate.

‘I was trying to be around the team, to help in any way I could.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It wasn’t really about the national service. Everyone was playing for the team, the country and the fans.

‘We managed to get the victory. Being exempt from national service was just a bonus, I guess.

‘The celebrations were enjoyable. It’s the first time my national team have won the Asian Games.

It has been revealed that ‘It was really hard — especially the game against Japan. It was a great achievement.’.

  • Sorrentino 6.5 - Sui gol non ha responsabilità, ma è bravissimo su Tutino e nelle uscite tenendo a galla i suoi davanti alle occasioni doriane.
  • Carissoni 5 - Perde Mezzotero nell’occasione del gol del vantaggio, ingenuità grave la sua, che poi non riesce a rialzarsi, giocando una partita piuttosto anonima.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Termina 1-2 allo Stadio Euganeo tra Padova e Sampdoria nella 13ª giornata di Serie BKT. A decidere la sfida la doppietta di Mezzotero per i blucerchiati. In mezzo la rete di Giunti.

Sorrentino 6.5 - Sui gol non ha responsabilità, ma è bravissimo su Tutino e nelle uscite tenendo a galla i suoi davanti alle occasioni doriane.

Carissoni 5 - Perde Mezzotero nell’occasione del gol del vantaggio, ingenuità grave la sua, che poi non riesce a rialzarsi, giocando una partita piuttosto anonima.

Silletti 5.5 - Gara affidabile la sua, contiene bene Tutino, che comunque riesce a creare la migliore occasione del match dopo i gol.

Pastina 5.5 - Soffre la qualità dell’attacco doriano, dalla sua parte arriva il gol del vantaggio.

According to recent reports, zanimacchia 6.5 - Da quella parte è un fattore. Quando sgasa e parte non lo si prende e i suoi cross sono spesso e volentieri insidiosissimi. Dal 70’ Capelli 5.5 - Non riesce ad essere efficace come il compagno che ha rilevato.

Giunti 6.5 - Si trova al posto giusto al momento giusto, insaccando il tiro sbilenco, diventato assist, di Fusi. Dall’80’ Cocchi sv.

According to recent reports, fusi 6 - Tanto dinamismo e voglia nella sua partita. Ci abbina anche un assist, quasi sicuramente involontario, a coronare una prestazione buona, macchiata solamente dal giallo che gli farà saltare la prossima. Dal 70’ Zuelli 5.5 - Ha sui piedi un’occasione potenziale quando calcia al volo in area, trovando però una deviazione che gli nega qualsiasi velleità di gol.

Pompetti 5.5 - Si spende moltissimo, ma è spesso fuori dal gioco, poco coinvolto nella manovra.

Varas 5.5 - Si fa trovare spesso e volentieri nell’area di rigore avversaria, invadendo e cercando di creare superiorità con i suoi inserimenti. Ha un paio di occasioni, ma le vanifica. Dall’85’ Bortolussi sv.

Seghetti 5.5 - Svaria moltissimo nel fronte offensivo, ma questo lo porta via dall’area. Il risultato è che l’attaccante in zona gol si vede pochissimo. Dall’80’ Di Mariano sv.

Moro 4.5 - Ha sulla testa un’occasione colossale quando stacca da solo sul cross di Zanimacchia. Un errore pesante, che costa almeno un punto ai suoi.

Allenatore: Padovano (Calabro squalificato) 5.5 - Il Padova parte male, poi ritorna e domina per larghi tratti con un palleggio più che convincente. Nel finale però si scioglie e perde una partita che avrebbe potuto anche vincere.

Industry observers note that krastev 6 - Non ha colpe sul gol. Poi quando viene chiamato in causa, risponde presente senza essere costretto a grandi interventi.

Mbabu 6.5 - Mette a referto un altro assist con un cross dolcissimo per la testa di Mezzotero. Dalla sua parte arrivano i maggiori pericoli. Mette in campo tutta la sua esperienza e si rende utilissimo alla squadra. Peccato per l’infortunio che gli fa chiudere anzitempo la gara. Dal 75’ Lauritsen sv.

Ravanelli 6 - Solido. Copre bene su Seghetti e Moro, senza soffrire la velocità nella manovra biancorossa.

According to recent reports, delli Carri 6 - Inizio di gara impacciato e lento. Poi cresce, ma soffre sempre in marcatura su Moro. Nel finale è bravo a spazzare ogni pericolo.

Meijer 5.5 - Da quella parte Zanimacchia gli fa venire il mal di testa: è alla prima da titolare e deve entrare in ritmo. D’Angelo infatti gli concede solo un tempo. Dal 46’ Gartenmann 6 - Entra e il Padova non crea più i pericoli del primo tempo. Adattato da terzino si comporta comunque benissimo.

Makoumbou 6 - Abbina corsa e contrasti inseguendo chiunque gli si pari davanti, sbaglia forse troppo con la palla tra i piedi, toccandola troppe volte e rallentando la manovra.

Abildgaard 6 - Mediano nel centrocampo di D’Angelo, smista bene ed è bravo nei contrasti, aiutando molto i difensori.

Henderson 5.5 - Gara di sostanza, macchiata da un giallo ingenuo, che gli farà saltare l’importante sfida contro la Cremonese. Dal 71’ Depaoli sv.

Mezzotero 7 - Segna un gol da attaccante purissimo girando di testa un bel cross di Mbabu, poi bissa avvitandosi e calciando in porta sul servizio di Insigne. Ai due gol abbina tecnica e fisicità al servizio della squadra. Partita totale la sua: ne sentiremo parlare.

According to recent reports, tutino 6 - Svaria tantissimo nel fronte offensivo, scambia bene con i compagni e fa sudare i suoi marcatori. Ha anche una grande palla gol per il 2-1, ma Sorrentino lo ipnotizza. Dal 63’ Insigne 6.5 - Cambia la partita con la sua enorme qualità. Prima accende.

Begic 6 - Vivace, ma troppo fumoso nell’ultima decisione. Quando si accende trova spesso la superiorità per i suoi, ma non è lucido nelle scelte. Dal 71’ Verschaeren sv.

It has been revealed that allenatore: D’Angelo 6.5 - La sua Sampdoria parte benissimo: pressing alto e verticalità mettono in grande crisi il Padova. Poi cala fisiologicamente dal punto di vista fisico, ma nel finale trova energie insperate anche grazie ai cambi, che permettono ai suoi di centrare il quarto successo di fila.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il club festeggerà il 3 dicembre con un allenamento a porte aperte; la divisa celebrativa è limitata a 1906 esemplari.

Il Torino farà debuttare la maglia celebrativa dei suoi 120 anni sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, nella partita contro la Lazio al Grande Torino. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, La divisa, realizzata con Joma per la stagione 2026/27, sarà prodotta in 1906 esemplari, ciascuno con un numero seriale sul fronte.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that il club granata celebrerà l’anniversario il 3 dicembre anche con un allenamento a porte aperte allo stadio Olimpico. La società presenta così la nuova divisa: «Nella stagione del 120º anniversario del Club, Torino FC e Joma presentano una maglia speciale per la stagione 2026/27: un'edizione celebrativa che riprende alcuni segni dell'identità granata con uno sguardo rivolto al presente e all’innovazione».

L’esordio in Torino-Lazio aprirà le iniziative legate alla ricorrenza. Nel comunicato, il club spiega: «La maglia celebrativa farà il suo esordio al Grande Torino sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, in occasione di Torino-Lazio e darà il via alle iniziative che accompagneranno il Club fino a giovedì 3 dicembre e oltre».

Sources indicate that il riferimento al Filadelfia e agli anni Ottanta accompagna il significato attribuito alla divisa: «Dal Filadelfia allo stadio, dagli anni Ottanta a oggi: questa maglia non chiede di guardare indietro, ma di celebrare le nostre radici nel presente. Ci ricorda che la Storia e la tradizione del Toro vivranno per sempre, grazie a chi continua a indossare questo colore e a tenere accesa la fede Granata».

L’edizione è limitata a «soli 1906 pezzi», in richiamo all’anno di fondazione del Torino. Ogni esemplare porta il proprio numero seriale sul fronte. Sul granata acceso, sottili linee bianche riprendono la trama di una maglia da allenamento usata negli anni Ottanta al Filadelfia, dove si preparava la partita del fine settimana.

According to recent reports, il comunicato descrive il passaggio di quella trama dal campo d’allenamento alla nuova divisa, reinterpretata in chiave contemporanea. Sulla maglia compare il toro rampante degli anni Ottanta, indicato dal club come un simbolo capace di unire generazioni diverse di tifosi attraverso i racconti e la passione di nonni e genitori.

According to recent reports, una patch dorata dall’effetto cangiante celebra l’anniversario. Secondo la luce e il punto di vista, la scritta “Edizione limitata”, il logo e il numero 120 lasciano spazio al numero seriale del singolo capo. Lo stemma con il toro rampante è ricamato sul petto, all’altezza del cuore; il 120 ricompare sui bordi delle maniche, realizzati in tessuto elastico a coste. All’interno del colletto è stampata la data di fondazione: 3 dicembre 1906.

A pochi minuti dall'inizio della sfida contro lo Stoccarda, ai microfoni di Sky Sport ha parlato il presidente dell'Inter Beppe Marotta:.

"Non si finisce mai di imparare, bisogna sempre fare esperienza".

Stasera l'obbligo della vittoria.

According to recent reports, "Stasera dobbiamo tentare di vincere a tutti i costi. Come vedete questo nuovo format porta a posizioni imprevedibili. Importante fare risultato".

Rinnovo Carlos Augusto praticamente fatto, per Calhanoglu e Thuram c'è ancora da lavorare.

"Abbiamo a che fare con professionisti e ragazzi legati a questi colori, sono molto seri e tutti vogliono proseguire con noi. Ci sono tutti i presupposti, pur affrontando con calma queste situazioni, li porteremo tutti a risultato positivo. Sono dinamiche che non è che capitano solo all'Inter, in tutte le squadre si parla di rinnovi in questo periodo".

"Sono presente quasi tutti i giorni. Io sono con i ragazzi, vicino, ma c'è rispetto dei ruoli. Presenza silenziosa e importante, la società è sempre con loro. Li ho salutati come sempre, il lavoro principale l'ha svolto l'allenatore".

"Giocatore che non piace solo all'Inter, ma a tante squadre. Vista la vicinanza, normale che i miei direttori sportivi vadano a vederlo. Sorpresa importante per la nostra Serie A".

Published: 15:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 22 November 2026.

Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.

Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.

Industry observers note that well, if he did, it has taken them headlong into another cul-de-sac. That’s how it felt at Easter Road yesterday when they were trounced 4-0 by Dundee United and left second-bottom of the Premiership table with more than a third of the season completed.

It made rather a mockery of the club’s social media channels, the profile pages of which proudly trumpet their newfound status as ‘Premier Sports Cup finalists’… with an exclamation mark and a golden trophy emoji thrown in for good measure.

Sources indicate that self-respecting Hibs fans won’t be fooled by the propaganda. Not after a humiliating afternoon on which their much-vaunted anthem, ’Sunshine on Leith’, was belted out by a gleeful away support at Easter Road.

Long before Zac Sapsford’s first-half double and strikes after the interval by Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall, some supporters were digging out their anti-board banners and using a megaphone to voice their frustration with those upstairs.

Malky Mackay is under growing pressure from supporters in his role as Hibs sporting director.

Zac Sapsford scores the first of Dundee United 's four goals against Hibs at Easter Road.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley notes that he alone was to blame for their 8-0 thrashing by Hearts.

This is how it works at struggling clubs, where fans need someone to blame. First, they target players. Then they single out the manager. When his replacement proves to be no more effective, they have little option but to turn their guns on the board.

Recent findings suggest that not that there’s anything wrong with holding the hierarchy to account if they are the common denominator in a lengthy period of under-achievement. There has been little sign of progress at Easter Road since Bournemouth owner Bill Foley sold his Hibs shares back to the Gordon family last year, having suggested that they didn’t listen to his input. Big questions are also being asked of sporting director Malky Mackay who was asked in 2024 to lead and oversee the entire football operation, including recruitment and the appointment of a head coach.

It has been revealed that club legend David Gray had his moments as manager, but in the end, supporters wanted rid. Reedijk may turn out to be the real deal but the early signs are that he is struggling with the squad he has inherited. Too many of them failed to do the basics yesterday.

Industry observers note that unlike Hibs, Jim Goodwin’s Dundee United are a strong side with a clear identity. Not for nothing have they gone eight games without defeat, but they scored all too easily as they racked up their biggest-ever victory at Easter Road.

Hibs’ squad appears to be weak, imbalanced and too full of ill-advised signings for Reedijk to make the kind of impact he would like. The holes in it are such that he recently opted to use Scotland defender Grant Hanley as an emergency centre-forward.

Reedijk needs to begin an overhaul of that playing staff in the January window, but how much power will be granted in that process? The Dutch coach has already hinted that he will not be given the final say when it comes to transfers.

The fans are nervous about another rebuild under Mackay and his recruitment staff, whose work in the summer window left a lot to be desired. Jason Kerr was a double-winner with St Johnstone, but he has cut a hapless figure at the back. Midfielder Azeem Abdulai, signed on a three-year contract from Leyton Orient, has made only four appearances, just one from the start. And then there is striker Nathan Lowe, on loan from Stoke City, who is struggling to adapt.

Mackay’s record is under heavy scrutiny. He is to be commended for making a profit of around £6million on striker Kieron Bowie, but why has there been no substantial replacement since the striker’s move to Italy nearly a year ago? Can he really argue that expensive signings such as Thibault Klidje and Ante Suto have been value for money?

A club of Hibs’ size, with those resources, should not be in the relegation zone. Nor should they be struggling so pitifully in their own stadium – they have lost nine of their last ten league games there and haven’t taken three points at home since April.

Which tees up nicely Dundee’s visit to Easter Road on Tuesday, not least because the Tayside club suffered a humiliation of their own this weekend. While Hibs were conceding four, Steven Pressley's side were shipping eight in a hammering by Hearts that has surely inflicted significant psychological damage.

To his great credit, Pressley insisted afterwards that he alone was to blame for his team’s wretched performance. That may have been true on the night, but over an extended period, a club’s fortunes tend to be shaped by decisions off the pitch. As Hibs have been finding out.

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

💡 Key Takeaways

  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most crucial positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the substantial difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

In a recent development, zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

In a recent development, it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

It has been revealed that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

According to recent reports, asked if Tottenham had made a massive mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi stated: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

Industry observers note that that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Industry observers note that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

According to recent reports, johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery noted. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

It has been revealed that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

Industry observers note that no wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Outstanding from the Villa keeper!

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Sums up the early battles so far.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

According to recent reports, savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

And we are underway in north London!

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball introduced to.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Sources indicate that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Oliver Glasner non usa giri di parole per descrivere la situazione trovata al Nottingham Forest. Alla vigilia della sfida di Premier League contro il Chelsea, l'allenatore austriaco ha ammesso che gli standard all'interno del club non erano all'altezza delle ambizioni della società, sottolineando la necessità di un cambiamento culturale. Il Forest occupa attualmente una posizione appena sopra la zona retrocessione, con appena due vittorie nelle prime undici giornate di campionato, e il tecnico ritiene che il percorso di crescita richiederà ancora tempo.

Glasner ha individuato nell'assenza di standard condivisi uno dei principali problemi del club. "La stabilità in un'azienda nasce dagli standard. Chiunque arrivi deve impegnarsi a rispettarli. Onestamente, quando sono arrivato non erano abbastanza alti", ha dichiarato. L'austriaco ha poi affrontato anche il tema dell'integrazione dei calciatori stranieri: "Abbiamo giocatori che sono qui da quattro anni e non parlano inglese. Se vai in Italia, dopo tre mesi i giocatori rilasciano già le interviste in italiano. Se voglio allenare in Inghilterra devo parlare inglese, se voglio allenare in Italia devo parlare italiano. Altrimenti, Oliver Glasner, se vuoi parlare nel tuo dialetto, resta a casa in Austria, dove tutti ti capiscono, ma da nessun'altra parte".

Recent findings suggest that L'allenatore ha ribadito che il progetto del Nottingham Forest è quello di diventare una squadra stabilmente in grado di lottare nella parte sinistra della classifica di Premier League. "Siamo ancora a qualche passo da quell'obiettivo, ma sappiamo quali passi dobbiamo compiere. Questa è una stagione di transizione: restiamo ambiziosi, ma ci sono ancora molti problemi da risolvere". Nei giorni scorsi Glasner ha inoltre incontrato a Londra il proprietario Evangelos Marinakis per pianificare il mercato di gennaio. "Mi ha chiesto di cosa abbiamo bisogno per migliorare la squadra, lo staff e l'ambiente. Vuole il meglio per il Nottingham Forest. È stato un incontro molto positivo e ne è valsa la pena affrontare sei ore di viaggio", ha concluso il tecnico.
